newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed mostly lower in quiet trade. October closed at $350.10, down $2.40 a tonne, while December finished down $1.40 at $344.60. In New York raw sugar futures closed at the day's highs, buoyed by trade buying which emerged once selling dried up and the October contract failed to test support at 11.55 cents/lb. Support remained between 11.55 and 11.53 cents/lb basis October, trade sources said. There were no fresh news to influence prices.

EUROPE - During the week ended August 27, rains were recorded in most West European sugar beet areas. This ended the dryness in the United Kingdom and northern France. The eastern areas are still too dry. In the former Soviet Union sugar beet areas received the much needed rainfall and rain receipts for the month have returned to normal in nearly all areas. Only the central Volga valley and Central Black Soils still have very limited rain receipts.

UKRAINE - The third Ukrainian sugar beet test published by Reuters confirms that the country is in for a bad crop. The increase in beet yield was again unsatisfactory and the total at the end of August was not more than 19.20 tonnes, 19 percent less than last year. The sugar yield per ha reached 2.61 tonnes, 23 percent less than last year and 15 percent below the 1994 figure. The unfavourable beet test results and the 4 percent decline in the area sown to sugar beet point to a significantly lower crop in 1996/97.

GERMANY - Sugar imports in April 1996 amounted to 28,734 tonnes, raw value, up from 15,431 tonnes imported in April 1995. This brought cumulative imports in the first seven months of 1995/96 (October/April) up to 130,259 tonnes against 122,615 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1994/95 amounted to 225,848 tonnes compared to 213,664 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in 1995/96 were France with 96,727 tonnes whites compared to 88,708 tonnes and the Netherlands with 9,024 tonnes against 7,804 tonnes. Sugar exports in April 1996 amounted to 86,880 tonnes compared to 104,492 tonnes in April 1995. This brought cumulative exports in October/April 1995/96 up to 964,668 tonnes, up from 860,165 tonnes exported in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 1.45 million tonnes compared to 1.92 million tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in October/April 1995/96 were the United Arab Emirates with 111,453 tonnes whites compared to 111,007 tonnes, Belgium-Luxembourg with 106,655 tonnes against 68,427 tonnes and Switzerland with 63,615 tonnes against 59,165 tonnes.

TAIWAN - Sugar imports in May 1996 amounted to 31,020 tonnes, almost unchanged from the tonnage imported in the like month the previous year (31,500 tonnes). This brought cumulative imports in the first seven months of 1995/96 (November/May) up to 61,033 tonnes compared to 63,841 tonnes in 1994/95. Total imports in 1994/95 reached 125,386 tonnes against 32,774 tonnes in 1993/94. The major country of origin in November/May 1995/96 was Australia with 61,000 tonnes raw sugar. Sugar exports in November/May 1995/96 amounted to 20,355 tonnes against 14,771 tonnes in 1994/95. The major country of destination in November/May 1995/96 was the USA with 20,329 tonnes raws.
